extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, scientists, and educated readers seeking a methodological guide to investigating nature (early-modern/philosophy of science audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts Francis Bacon's methodological prescriptions for investigating nature: how to conduct experiments, form axioms by induction, and avoid cognitive and linguistic errors (the 'idols'). A guide to producing reliable natural-philosophical inquiry rather than rhetorical or purely logical disputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine degrees of certainty; restore senses to their former rank
rubrics_metrics.description: Our method consists in determining the degrees of certainty, restoring the senses to their former rank, and opening a new and certain course for the mind from the first actual perceptions of the senses themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin inquiry from actual sensory perceptions and assess how certain conclusions are; avoid beginning from preconceived abstract principles. This is set against relying on late-stage logic as a remedy for error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use instruments and mechanical aids to extend the understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects are produced by the means of instruments and helps, which the understanding requires no less than the hand; as instruments promote or regulate the motion of the hand, so those that are applied to the mind prompt or protect the understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect the unaided mind to discover deep effects; employ experimental apparatus and systematic aids to extend sensory reach and rigor. Example anti-pattern: attempting great intellectual results by mere meditation without instruments or method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin inquiry anew and direct the mind from first perceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: We must begin the whole labor of the mind again; not leaving it to itself, but directing it perpetually from the very first, and attaining our end as it were by mechanical aid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject simply polishing existing doctrines; restart methodology by guiding mental operations from sense-data rather than inherited systems. Avoid using logic as a late corrective for false premises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on genuine induction rather than confused abstractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Our only hope, then, is in genuine induction. If the notions which form the basis of the whole be confused and carelessly abstracted from things, there is no solidity in the superstructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form axioms by systematic abstraction from many particulars (not by speculative generalization). Treat induction as the central method for discovery rather than as rhetorical justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct axioms by ascending continually from sensible particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: There are but two ways of investigating truth: the true way constructs its axioms from the senses and particulars, by ascending continually and gradually, till it finally arrives at the most general axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build knowledge stepwise from ordered collections of instances; avoid leaping to grand generalities early. The proper method runs 'duly and regularly through' particulars rather than touching them cursorily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid anticipations (rash anticipations of the mind) and premature generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: We call that human reasoning which we apply to nature the anticipation of nature (as being rash and premature), and that which is properly deduced from things the interpretation of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not adopt axioms inferred from a few or familiar instances; such 'anticipations' enforce assent without being grounded in broad experience. Anti-pattern: declaring universal laws from limited, familiar cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on syllogism for discovery; it forces assent rather than truth
rubrics_metrics.description: The present system of logic... is useless for the discovery of the sciences. The syllogism forces assent, therefore, and not things; it is of no avail in intermediate axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use formal syllogistic reasoning for exposition or persuasion, not as the primary engine to discover natural principles. Beware of confounding logical consequence with empirical truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek causes in subordinate objects, not merely in greatest generalities or final causes
rubrics_metrics.description: He would be an unskilful and shallow philosopher who should seek for causes in the greatest generalities, and not be anxious to discover them in subordinate objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate proximate mechanisms and particular processes; avoid defaulting to teleological explanations (final causes) or overly remote, abstract causes that do not aid practical discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against the Idols of the Tribe
rubrics_metrics.description: The idols of the Tribe are inherent in human nature; man’s sense is falsely asserted to be the standard of things, and the human mind resembles uneven mirrors which distort and disfigure objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize species-level cognitive biases: tendency to impose human-centered order, to overgeneralize from limited perception, and to be deceived by the senses' limitations. Correct by systematic checks and reliance on varied instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against the Idols of the Den
rubrics_metrics.description: The idols of the Den are those of each individual: education, habit, disposition, reading, and preoccupations that intercept and corrupt the light of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of personal prejudices and specialized attachments (e.g., career-long focus leading to distorted interpretation). Encourage self-skepticism, rotation of perspectives, and methods that expose individual blind spots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against the Idols of the Market
rubrics_metrics.description: Idols of the Market arise from the commerce and association of men by language; words, when ill-formed, obstruct the mind and lead to controversies and fallacies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid letting popular language or sloppy vocabulary dictate conceptual frameworks; prefer clear definitions tied to instances. Anti-pattern: debates that are merely verbal quibbles rather than empirical disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against the Idols of the Theatre
rubrics_metrics.description: Idols of the Theatre are crept in from dogmas of systems of philosophy and perverted rules of demonstration; systems are like plays creating fictitious worlds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat whole philosophical systems with suspicion when they impose fictive frameworks unsupported by ordered observation. Do not refute systems merely by argument; instead expose them by empirical method and new instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer negative instances; negatives are most powerful for testing axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the peculiar and perpetual error of the human understanding to be more moved by affirmatives than negatives, whereas in establishing any true axiom the negative instance is the most powerful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tests that seek counterexamples; a single negative instance can overturn a false generality. Anti-pattern: collecting confirming examples only and ignoring disconfirming evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work from particular instances and their regular series and order
rubrics_metrics.description: We must bring men to particulars and their regular series and order... and they must for a while renounce their notions, and begin to form an acquaintance with things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize experiments and observations into orderly series; derive generalities only after systematic, comparative study of many cases. Practical guidance: gather varied, arranged instances rather than isolated anecdotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not base axioms on scanty experience; penetrate remote and secret parts of nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The axioms now in use are derived from a scanty handful... It is necessary to penetrate the more secret and remote parts of nature, in order to abstract both notions and axioms from things by a more certain and guarded method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek evidence beyond common, familiar occurrences; explore less-obvious phenomena to avoid biased axioms. Anti-pattern: generalizing from frequent but shallow observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use careful definitions and beware of confused words
rubrics_metrics.description: Words are generally formed in a popular sense... when a more acute understanding is anxious to vary those lines, words oppose it. There are names of things which have no existence, and names of actual objects but confused and badly defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie terms to clear, testable instances and avoid vague abstractions (e.g., 'moist' with multiple inconsistent meanings). Prefer operational or instance-based definitions when possible to reduce verbal idolatry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate analysis and synthesis; interchange attention to particulars and generals
rubrics_metrics.description: The contemplation of nature... in individual form distracts and weakens the understanding; but the contemplation of nature... in their general composition stupefies and relaxes it. These two species of contemplation must be interchanged, and each employed in its turn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance detailed examination of particulars (analysis) with efforts to synthesize broader patterns, using each in turn to avoid the extremes of narrowness or vague generality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instauration must begin from the foundations rather than patching old systems
rubrics_metrics.description: It is in vain to expect any great progress in the sciences by the superinducing or ingrafting new matters upon old. An instauration must be made from the very foundations, if we do not wish to revolve forever in a circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When foundational errors persist, prefer methodological reconstruction to incremental addition. Avoid ad hoc fixes that retain erroneous first principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct depraved habits of mind by seasonable hesitation and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Will correct the depraved and deeply rooted habits of his mind by a seasonable, and, as it were, just hesitation: and then, finally (if he will), use his judgment when he has begun to be master of himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate intellectual self-discipline: deliberate, suspend premature assent, and train judgment through experience and methodical practice. This is a procedural prescription for the inquirer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid extremes of dogmatism and of total scepticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who have presumed to dogmatize... have inflicted the greatest injury on philosophy... Those who assert that nothing can be known... have certainly adduced reasons; but they have exceeded due moderation. The ancient mean was to put it to the test of experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject both arrogant certainty and blanket denial of knowledge; pursue experiential testing and modest claims grounded in ordered induction rather than rhetorical victory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design apt experiments and let the senses judge the experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: All the better interpretations of nature are worked out by instances, and fit and apt experiments, where the senses only judge of the experiment, the experiment of nature and the thing itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize well-designed, relevant experiments judged by sensory or instrument-augmented observation. Anti-pattern: poor or irrelevant experiments that do not directly test the hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissect rather than abstract; study matter, conformation, and laws of action
rubrics_metrics.description: The human understanding is, by its own nature, prone to abstraction... It is better to dissect than abstract nature... It is best to consider matter, its conformation, and the changes of that conformation, its own action, and the law of this action or motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on concrete mechanisms and dynamics (dissection, experimental manipulation) instead of inventing speculative 'forms' detached from material processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of confirmation bias and the mind's inclination to force agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The human understanding, when any proposition has been once laid down... forces everything else to add fresh support and confirmation... it is more moved and excited by affirmatives than negatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively seek counterexamples and resist the tendency to reinterpret or dismiss disconfirming data. Methods: blind testing, independent replication, explicit search for negative instances.
